text: Is my easy pace too fast?

No, your easy pace looks fine. Your prescribed easy band is 5:11-6:13/km, and your easy runs sit mid-band: 5:42 on 11-05, 5:44 on 11-12, 5:48 on 11-14 and 5:46 on 11-21. The 4-week average is 5:47/km at HR 141. That is about 75% of your 188 max, which is genuinely aerobic, and the HR is steady within each run with even splits.

The one thing I'd watch is the long runs. HR rose from 142 on 11-08 (5:47/km) to 143 on 11-15 (5:50/km) and 146 on 11-22 (5:52/km), and efficiency fell from 1.218 to 1.169. That is a small drift, and it comes after your biggest week so far, so it is a note and not a reason to change anything. If the next long run shows HR climbing again at the same pace, slow down a little rather than speed up.

One gap in the data: I see nothing logged since the 11-22 long run, so the Tuesday 11-24 easy run and strength session aren't recorded. If you did them, log them so I can keep an accurate picture.

text: Swap Thursday and Saturday next week please, I'm travelling Thursday.

I can't do a straight Thursday/Saturday swap in week 5. That would put the 4 x 0.8 km intervals on Sat 12-05 and the long run on Sun 12-06, which are back-to-back hard days. Putting the intervals on Wednesday doesn't work either, because Tuesday's tempo would sit right before them.

What I would propose instead: keep Tue 12-01 as the tempo and keep the Sunday long run. Wed 12-02 becomes an easy 8 km run in place of the ride. Thursday is off for travel. Sat 12-05 stays an easy 8 km, with Strength B moved there from Thursday. The interval session drops out of that week, and so does the ride, since there is no free day for it. Losing one interval session is a small cost. Your fitness is steady (CTL 46.4) and your tempos are on target (4:36-4:37/km), so I wouldn't force the intervals in.

If you'd rather keep the intervals, tell me and I'll look at making Tuesday the interval day instead of the tempo. The proposal will be prepared separately for you to accept or decline.
